about: The task-name limit and its boundary. Each case types `prefix` (absent means empty), then `repeat` written `count` times, then `suffix`, into a fresh app's Add Task composer and presses Add. `accepted: true` means the edit lands and Add creates one task whose name is the typed text trimmed; false means the edit is refused as typed, so the draft stays empty and Add creates nothing. The unit is the Unicode scalar value: Rust counts str::chars, the web host counts code points, never String.length. task-mosaic-app's native test and the web host's test both run every case and both check their limit equals `maxChars`, so the hosts cannot drift apart. Astral and combining characters are written as \u escapes.

cases.name: two-byte, at the cap (1,024 UTF-8 bytes: not a byte cap)
astral, at the cap (1,024 UTF-16 units: String.length would refuse it)
an astral last character reaches the cap
an astral character one past the cap
scalars, not graphemes: e + combining acute is two
scalars, not graphemes: one more scalar is past the cap
the draft is measured as typed: a leading space counts
the draft is measured untrimmed, the name stored trimmed
